title: Conversation unit of work is not one transaction
claim: The product application service opens an ILlmChatUnitOfWork, but EfLlmConversationStore creates a separate AppDbContext and transaction.
impact: Create can leave orphan product/transcript state; rename can commit two different titles.

title: Conversation title and transcript metadata have duplicate writable truth
claim: Product and transcript rows both carry mutable conversation metadata.
impact: Independent commits can diverge and every read must guess which row is authoritative.

title: Turn admission and evidence are split across commits
claim: ProfileFencedLlmConversationStore persists the conversation change, then invokes evidence callbacks through another unit of work.
impact: A crash or evidence failure can leave an active transcript turn without matching operation evidence.

title: Assistant commit and terminal operation state are not atomic
claim: The provider result can be committed to the transcript before operation success is committed.
impact: A retry/recovery path may see a completed answer and a nonterminal or failed operation.

title: Compensation exhaustion is swallowed
claim: Compensation retries are bounded but exhaustion returns without establishing a durable RecoveryRequired outcome.
impact: A Failed or Cancelled operation can retain a live active turn that normal recovery refuses to abandon.

title: Committed cancellation can still become success
claim: CompleteTranscript accepts CancellationRequested and finalization does not re-check durable cancellation in the same transaction.
impact: The state machine can report Succeeded after the caller durably cancelled before final commit.

title: Idempotent replay is gated by later mutable lifecycle state
claim: Definition/conversation eligibility is checked before resolving an existing operation and its fingerprint.
impact: A successful request may stop replaying after the definition is suspended or the conversation archived.

title: Profile fence does not cover the complete use case
claim: The runtime lease surrounds conversation engine/provider work, while metadata reads/writes happen outside it.
impact: One request can combine metadata, provider, and commits from different profile generations.

title: Running ownership and cancellation are process-local
claim: The cancellation/running registry is in memory and reconciliation uses local presence as liveness evidence.
impact: A second app instance can recover a live operation owned by the first; cross-instance cancellation is ineffective.

title: HTTP request lifetime owns paid execution
claim: The send endpoint awaits provider execution inline using the request cancellation token.
impact: Client disconnects and slow local LLMs produce accidental cancellation and poor external-client behavior.

title: Attempt audit does not represent actual attempts consistently
claim: The audit wrapper records ordinal 1 while the provider adapter may perform more than one dispatch attempt.
impact: Usage, retry, and recovery evidence cannot reconstruct the actual dispatch sequence.

title: Timeout and cancellation reduce differently before and after restart
claim: DeadlineExceeded is written as Cancelled in invocation audit but handled as a failed deadline by the direct request path.
impact: The same durable evidence can yield a different terminal operation state after reconciliation.

title: Conversation and transcript reads are unbounded or in-memory paged
claim: The EF conversation store materializes the full transcript and list paths build summaries from full documents.
impact: Long-running enterprise chats and chatbot traffic create memory, latency, and N+1 growth.

title: Archive can race active work
claim: Archive does not atomically reject an active turn or nonterminal operation.
impact: A conversation may be archived while a provider answer is being admitted or finalized.

title: Provider contracts and drivers have no true streaming path
claim: IProviderChatCompletionDriver exposes only CompleteChatAsync; OpenAI/Azure use completed HTTP responses and Ollama sends stream=false.
impact: An SSE endpoint alone could only poll or fake progressive output.

title: HTTP origin is caller-controlled and dedicated LLM scopes are missing
claim: Conversation creation accepts an Origin field and the API family lacks distinct read/manage/execute policy names.
impact: Audit provenance can be spoofed and remotely enabled authorization is less granular than required for enterprise/external clients.

title: Committed closure and branch provenance are not release-ready
claim: The feature branch is behind development, has no workflow run at its head, and the original bundle records a red stable gate.
impact: The next wave would rely on stale or incomplete proof and an unsynchronized baseline.
